neet_phy_u08_t03_1.working: In an adiabatic process Q = 0, so W = -ΔU. Expansion work is positive, so ΔU < 0 and the temperature falls.

neet_phy_u08_t03_2.working: W = nRT ln(P1/P2) = 1 × 8.3 × 300 × ln 10 = 2490 × 2.303 ≈ 5734 J ≈ 5.73 kJ, positive because the gas does work on expansion.

neet_phy_u08_t03_4.working: Isothermal: ΔT = 0 with Q ≠ 0, so C is infinite (A-II). Adiabatic: Q = 0, so C = 0 (B-III). Adiabatic bulk modulus = γP (C-I). Slope ratio, adiabatic to isothermal = γ (D-IV).

neet_phy_u08_t03_5.working: A is false: the isothermal curve lies above the adiabatic, so isothermal work is greater. B is true for a rigid diatomic gas (γ = 7/5). C is true since ΔU = 0, so Q = W. D is true since W = -ΔU = nCv(T1 - T2). E is false: an adiabatic process needs insulating walls or a fast process.
